findings.element: Tasks · .board grid (tasks.board and tasks.compact, WAITING collapsed) at viewports ≥ 1811px
findings.problem: The board's grid computes to `372px 372px 372px 172px 372px` at 1920. The four content lanes are clamped at their 372px ceiling and the 200px the collapsed WAITING lane hands back is never redistributed, so the tracks total 1660 inside a 1770px content box. Measured: board content right edge 1886, last tray right edge 1776 — 110px of dead white. The right-hand alignment the surface otherwise keeps to the pixel breaks with it: .headActions and .viewTools both end at 1874 while the last card ends at 1764. That contract holds exactly at 1280 (1234/1234), 1440 (1394/1394), 1600, 1750 and 1810, then breaks 40px at 1850, 110px at 1920 and 200px at 2048 and above. The left edge stays perfect at 128 throughout, so the board reads as pushed left; the dock, which is centred on the sheet (centre 1001), then sits 55px off the centre of the board it floats over (occupied centre 946). tasks.dense, with no empty lane, fills to the content edge at every width — the grid is capable of this. The CSS's own comment states the intent it fails: "an empty lane on a populated board is a rail rather than a fifth of the sheet ... and the four lanes with work in them take the room." 1920 is the width every hero frame in this lab is shot at.
findings.fix: Add one declaration beside the five existing `:has()` collapse rules at _gate-suite.html:1837-1841, raising the content lanes' ceiling by exactly the room the collapse returns (372 + (372-172)/4 = 422): `[data-app="tasks"] .board:not([data-filtered]):not([data-blank]):has(> .tray[data-empty]) { --lane: minmax(196px, 422px); }`. Verified by injection: the break goes to 0 at 1200, 1280, 1440, 1810, 1920, 2048 and 2560; tracks at 1920 become 399.5/399.5/399.5/172/399.5; no new horizontal scroll at any width.

findings.element: Tasks · .board.listBoard bottom reserve, every width from 768 to 1199 where the list is the view and the dock floats
findings.problem: `.board.listBoard` reserves `padding: 0 25px 28px`. The card board next to it reserves `padding: 0 16px 84px` and its comment says why: "48px of dock plus 18px of inset plus the float shadow's reach." 28px is not that. Driven at 768x1024 with the list scrolled to the true end of its scroller (nothing further to reveal): the dock's band is y 922→970 and the last row sits at y 917→953, so the final task's title and owner name are entirely inside the opaque dock. Only its tick, its DONE pip and its 2 Jul chip survive, one either side of the pill. Reproduced identically at 768x900, 900x800, 1024x800, 1180x800 and 1199x900 — the whole band where the list is the default view. The phone is clean (the dock is a separate band below the sheet there) and the card board is clean at 1280 and 1920, so this is the one place the reserve was written twice and only once correctly.
findings.fix: Give the list the board's own reserve and keep the board's own phone exception. At _gate-suite.html:1633 change `padding: 0 25px 28px` to `padding: 0 25px 84px`, and add `@media (max-width: 720px) { [data-app="tasks"] .board.listBoard { padding-bottom: 14px; } }` (there is no dock on a phone, matching the note at line 3617). Verified by injection at 768: scrollHeight 1074→1130, last row bottom 928 against a dock top of 946 — the same 18px clearance the board gives.

findings.element: Tasks · .lrow .tick in List view — the default view below 1200 and the only view on a phone
findings.problem: The fill that marks a completed task is scoped to the card only: `[data-app="tasks"] .card[data-done] .tick { background: var(--ink); box-shadow: none; color: var(--white); }` (line 2326). There is no `.lrow[data-done] .tick` counterpart, and the base `.tick` is `color: transparent` over a 1.4px ink-28 ring. Measured across all 13 rows at 1024x900 (8 open, 5 done): identical transparent background, identical `rgba(17,17,17,0.28)` ring and identical transparent check glyph on every one; only `aria-checked` differs. Driven: clicking an open row's tick flips `data-done`, turns the lane word to DONE, greens the pip and fades the title to 62% ink — and the circle under the pointer stays an empty ring. `.card[data-just-done]` carries the settle and check-draw animations; `.lrow` has no equivalent, so there is no moment of completion at all. The leftmost column of the list — thirteen ticks, the fastest scan in a view whose own CSS comment says "scanning is the only reason to choose it over the board" — carries no information, and the product's most-pressed control is the one thing on screen that never shows its own state. The behaviour gate asserts the attribute flipped (interaction-check.mjs:314), never that the control paints.
findings.fix: Broaden the two existing card rules to cover the row, next to them. Line 2326 becomes `[data-app="tasks"] .card[data-done] .tick, [data-app="tasks"] .lrow[data-done] .tick { background: var(--ink); box-shadow: none; color: var(--white); }` and lines 3160-3161 become `[data-app="tasks"] .card[data-done] .tick:hover, [data-app="tasks"] .card[data-done] .tick:focus-visible, [data-app="tasks"] .lrow[data-done] .tick:hover, [data-app="tasks"] .lrow[data-done] .tick:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--wash-2); }`. Palette-safe: --ink on white with a --white glyph is the exact pair the card already ships and the audit already passes.

findings.problem: The page carries five horizontal rules. `.tl-paperEdge`, `.b-behind` and `.b-foot` are all `rgba(17,17,17,0.16)` and span the stage. The other two are both `rgb(79,70,229)`, 1px: `.b-rail`, which is the measure and runs 1120px at 1440 and 1600px at 1920, and `.b-todayRule`, which is `max-width: 344px` and measures exactly 344px at 1280, 1440 and 1920 alike. So the one surface in the suite whose entire argument is that horizontal length equals `daysFromToday × pixels-per-day` puts a second accent hairline 265px directly above its measure, in the same colour and the same weight, at a fixed length that encodes nothing and does not move while the measure below it grows by 480px. Every other divider on the page is an ink tint; this is the only one promoted to the accent, and it is the only one that is not a distance.
findings.fix: Change line 6592 from `background: var(--accent)` to `background: var(--fore-16)`, the ink tint the page's three other rules already use: `[data-app="timeline"] .b-todayRule { height: 1px; background: var(--fore-16); margin: var(--gap-block) 0 0; max-width: 344px; }`. One indigo horizontal line then remains on the surface and it is the measure. No new hue, no new weight.

findings.problem: The head's inset drops from 28px to 16px below 720, but `.board.listBoard { padding: 0 25px }` is never re-scoped, so the list stops sharing the column the head sits on. Measured wordmark-left vs tick-left, and head-actions-right vs row-meta-right: 768 → 116/117 and 728/728; 1024 → 128/129 and 978/978; 1199 → 128/129 and 1153/1153. The desk keeps the contract to a pixel. Then 390 → 25/40 and 365/350; 430 → 25/40 and 405/390; 600 → 25/40 and 575/560. On a 390px screen the wordmark, project name, progress line and segmented control all sit on 25/365 and the thirteen-row list directly beneath them sits on 40/350 — 15px inside on both sides, 4% of the screen's width, with the row hairlines ending short of the controls above them.
findings.fix: Re-scope the list's inset on the phone so 10px of scroller padding plus the row's own 6px lands on the head's 16px: add `@media (max-width: 720px) { [data-app="tasks"] .board.listBoard { padding-left: 10px; padding-right: 10px; } }` beside the existing 720 block at line 1740. Verified at 320, 390, 430 and 600: tick left becomes 25 (= wordmark left) and row meta right becomes 295/365/405/575 (= head actions right) at each; 768 and above are untouched; no horizontal scroll introduced at any width, 320 included.

biggestWin: The suite composes as one object, and it does so by measurement rather than by resemblance. At 1920 all three products hang their sheet on the identical box — 100/18/18/18 on the ink floor — and all three resolve to the same optical centre to the pixel: Notes' 1120 stack and 1060 paper, Timeline's 1722 stage and the dock in both products all land on 1001. The rail capsule is the same discipline in miniature: 10px above the mark, 10px below the avatar, 10px either side of every tile, the avatar centred to the pixel at every width. And it survives being driven: narrowing one live page 1440 → 1200 → 1024 → 900 → 768 → 600 → 430 → 390 and back restores head, views, board, dock, segmented control, tools, head actions and every tray width EXACTLY, in all three products, with zero page errors — the composition is derived, not drawn twice. That is the thing that makes three products read as one application, and it is at the level of the benchmarks named in the brief.
